senses.sense_definition: An embarrassing or funny mistake made in public or during the recording of a film, television show, or radio broadcast, often preserved as an outtake.

examples.text: The end credits of the comedy movie featured a hilarious <w>blooper</w> reel of the actors forgetting their lines.
The news anchor laughed uncontrollably after making an embarrassing <w>blooper</w> on live television.

senses.sense_definition: An embarrassing, foolish, or conspicuous blunder or error.

examples.text: Printing the wrong date on thousands of event invitations was a major <w>blooper</w> by the design team.
He tried to laugh off his embarrassing <w>blooper</w> during the formal business presentation.

senses.sense_definition: A weakly hit fly ball that drops into the outfield just beyond the reach of the infielders.

examples.text: The batter managed to drive in two runs with a lucky <w>blooper</w> to shallow right field.
The outfielder sprinted forward but could not reach the falling <w>blooper</w> before it hit the grass.

senses.sense_definition: A lightweight, full-cut sail set opposite a spinnaker to provide additional power when running before the wind.

examples.text: The crew decided to hoist the <w>blooper</w> to gain extra speed on the downwind leg of the race.
When the wind shifted slightly, they had to ease the sheet and take down the <w>blooper</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A radio receiver that oscillates and radiates signals, causing loud squealing interference in nearby receivers.

examples.text: His homemade regenerative set acted as a <w>blooper</w> and ruined reception for everyone on the block.
Early radio regulations sought to eliminate any <w>blooper</w> that produced annoying feedback across neighborhoods.

senses.sense_definition: An M79 grenade launcher, known informally by this nickname due to the distinct sound it produces when fired.

examples.text: The soldier carried a <w>blooper</w> slung over his shoulder as the squad moved carefully through the dense jungle.
A single round from the <w>blooper</w> was enough to silence the enemy position on the ridge.
